headline: Committee votes on cost-saving choices for Malden River Works Salt Shed & Boathouse project, including roof, siding, and window materials.
summary: The committee discussed project financing and voted on several cost-saving design choices for the Salt Shed & Boathouse project, including storage racks, roof type, siding, and windows. All votes were unanimous. The committee also planned a meeting with high school coaches and Gentle Giant about boat storage needs, with the next committee meeting set for September 3.
decisions: Approved bidding the boat house storage racks as a deduct alternate, unanimous vote.
Approved including the salt shed in the base bid instead of as a deduct alternate, unanimous vote.
Approved using all wood siding for the boathouse, unanimous vote.
Approved moving forward with the corrugated metal roof, with the committee choosing the roof color/finish, unanimous vote.
Approved keeping the stick built storefront window system for the boathouse, unanimous vote.

Committee to Approve Minutes
Committee to approve the 6/25/26 and 7/9/26 meeting minutes.
 Amanda motioned to approve the minutes; Steve seconded the motion. The Committee voted 
unanimously to approve the minutes. 
Malden River Works Salt Shed & Boathouse Project Updates
Updates regarding project financing.
 Nelson explained that he spoke with Ron Hogan, who is in conversation with the Mayor’s Office 
about project financing. They’re working on a way to fill the funding gap.
Committee to discuss and vote on cost-saving project choices, including about the following:
 Boat house MC cable option
o Nelson talked to Malden’s wiring inspectors about this
o They said that the use of this building does not require conduit; it can be conventional

 Whether to include boat house storage racks in the bid
o Sam (designLAB) reiterated that either way, Malden could get the same product. It’s just
a matter of whether we treat the racks as a building element vs. furniture. We could buy
the racks direct from the vendor, which would allow the City to avoid paying a 
contractor’s markup.
o Marie (Landing Studio, sub to designLAB) noted that the current design plans for more 
racks than what the high school team needs, but the same amount as existed in the 
previous “tent” boathouse.
o Amanda noted that we should be assuming high-capacity storage needs/considering 
room to grow.
o Group agreed that either way, the boat racks will be needed immediately upon 
completion of construction.
o Steve motioned to bid the storage racks as a deduct alternate. Amanda seconded this. 
The group voted unanimously in favor of this approach. 
 Salt shed as a deduct alternate
o The group felt that taking this approach would fundamentally alter the bid, and noted 
that Malden really needs a salt shed.
o Steve motioned that the salt shed be included in the base bid, not as a deduct alternate.
Amanda seconded this. The group voted unanimously in favor of this approach.
 Boathouse siding options (see attached email for details)
o Sam clarified that the decision point here is whether to use aluminum or wood siding in 
the area where the coach’s office and bathrooms will be. The remainder of the 
boathouse is already planned as wood siding. Sam recommended that Malden choose 
to do all wood siding everywhere, as it will look cleaner, be easier to maintain (the 
maintenance is more gradual over time), and saves a little money. Sam noted that the 
insulation will remain the same.
o Steve motioned to accept Sam’s recommendation and use all wood siding for the 
boathouse. Amanda seconded this. The group voted unanimously in favor of this 
approach.
 Boathouse corrugated metal roof
o Steve asked about how corrugated metal roof ages over time, to which Sam responded 
that it performs similarly to a standing seam metal roof (which is the alternative option 
here).
o Sam noted that the advantage of a seam roof is that it’s more aesthetic and slightly 
more leak proof. However, he noted that for our boathouse, the roof is “low slope” so it 
won’t be as visible to park goers, and the building is “open air” so leaks are less of a 
concern. The corrugated metal, by contrast, is about $50,000 cheaper, still reliable, and 
simpler. Both options can be factory coated and the same color choices are available.
o Nelson noted that leaks do not concern him here, and ice dams will not be an issue with 
the corrugated metal roof. 
o Steve suggested that we could bid the seam roof but put a substitution for corrugated 
metal as a deduct alternate. Sam reminded the group that for alternates, we would 
need to determine the priority order and accept alternates in that order (i.e., you can’t 
just pick and choose the alternates you want).
o Steve motioned to move forward with the corrugated metal roof with the caveat that 
the committee would like to choose the roof color/finish to control for aesthetics. 
Amanda seconded this. The group voted unanimously in favor of this approach. 
 Boathouse storefront window system

o Sam reminded the group that the choice here is a “stick built” storefront window system
vs. a mulled window system where the glass comes already built into the frames. His 
recommendation was to keep the “stick built” storefront window system because the 
savings aren’t that great. 
o Nelson shared that in previous conversations, Eric Rubin was in favor of keeping the 
“stick built” system, too, for maintenance reasons, as it’s easier to replace the glass if it 
breaks.
o Steve motioned to keep the “stick built” storefront window system. Amanda seconded 
this. The group voted unanimously in favor of this approach. 
Invoice Approval
 There were no new invoices to approve. Sam noted that there was no need for a July invoice, so the next 
one will be for August services.
New Business
 Sam noted that with the decisions made today, his team is ready to move into Construction Drawings 
(CDs). They should be done by September 18.
 Sam will send a template for Division 0 documents and his team’s Division 1 documents for review.
 The group decided to arrange a virtual meeting with the high school coaches and Gentle Giant to confirm 
the number and type of boats that need to be accommodated in the boathouse. Amanda noted that the 
group should also ask these stakeholders about their interest in/goals for future expansion, so that the 
committee could keep this in mind as they make decisions. Bekah McPheeters will help to schedule this 
meeting.
 The next committee meeting is scheduled for September 3 at 12PM.
Adjournment
 Steve motioned to adjourn. Amanda seconded this. The group voted unanimously to adjourn at 12:56.
